summary: Iter-35 Binance Spot CCXT integration: backend HTTP smoke test pass. All 17 new HTTP tests pass + all 17 prior unit tests pass (34/34 total). Auth gates, validation, bad-keys rejection, defence-in-depth live toggle, and regression endpoints all verified.
critical_code_review_comments: crypto_routes.py POST /accounts catches Exception broadly during fetch_balance probe; consider narrowing to ccxt.AuthenticationError/NetworkError for clearer 422 vs 502 separation, but current 422-with-detail behaviour is acceptable for UX.
_serialize() decrypts api_key on every list call only for masking — fine for low cardinality (single-digit accounts per user) but could be cached if list size grows.

binance_engine.py line 156: account['_id'] used directly — assumes caller always passes a Mongo doc with _id; route layer satisfies this via _load_user_account, but the engine itself could KeyError if called from a future code path with a dict that omits _id. Defensive .get('_id') with explicit raise would be safer.
No rate limit on POST /api/crypto/accounts probe — a script could spam Binance via the sanity-fetch (and Binance will throttle/ban). Consider a per-user cooldown.
seed_data_creation: None — POST /crypto/accounts with garbage keys correctly rejects with 422 BEFORE persist, so no test rows created. Pre/post list-count assertion confirms no leak.
